skill.name: wp-plugin-development

content.value_statement: WordPress plugin work can create security, lifecycle, and packaging mistakes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured plugin changes, verification, and release preparation.
actual_capabilities: Locates WordPress plugin entry points by scanning PHP plugin headers.
Guides bootstrap structure, hook registration, and admin-only loading patterns.
Covers activation, deactivation, uninstall, migrations, and rewrite flush guardrails.
Supports Settings API work with sanitization, capability checks, and escaped output.
Reviews nonce use, request handling, prepared SQL, cron tasks, and release packaging.
limitations: It does not replace the WordPress Plugin Handbook or official plugin review.
Precise edits need repository access and a known target plugin path.
Some verification steps require WP-CLI, PHPUnit, PHPCS, or a local WordPress site.
Guidance follows the skill target of WordPress 6.9+ and PHP 7.2.24+.

use_cases.title: Refactor Plugin Architecture
use_cases.description: Restructure a plugin around a clear bootstrap file, loader class, and hook registration flow.

use_cases.title: Add Secure Admin Settings
use_cases.description: Create or update Settings API screens with capability checks, nonces, sanitization, and escaped output.

use_cases.title: Review Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Check lifecycle hooks, uninstall behavior, cron jobs, SQL safety, assets, and release packaging before publication.

prompt_templates.title: Find Plugin Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the WordPress plugin entry point in this repository. Summarize the plugin structure and identify the main files to inspect first.

prompt_templates.title: Add Settings Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a settings page for [option name]. Use the Settings API, capability checks, nonce handling, sanitization, and escaped output.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Hook Loading
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this plugin to separate bootstrap, hook registration, admin code, and service classes. Preserve behavior and list verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this plugin for release readiness. Check lifecycle hooks, uninstall cleanup, cron tasks, SQL safety, security controls, and packaging gaps.

output_examples.input: I need to add a settings page for an API key.
output: A Settings API plan with option names, capability requirements, and sanitization rules.
A focused implementation path for the admin page and save flow.
Verification steps for saving, loading, escaping, and permission checks.
A lifecycle review that checks where activation hooks are registered.
Likely causes such as missing dependencies, rewrite timing, or network activation assumptions.
A short test plan for activation, deactivation, and uninstall behavior.
A release checklist covering security, database changes, cron tasks, assets, and packaging.
A list of gaps that should be fixed before distribution.
Recommended local checks using the tools already present in the repository.

best_practices: Provide the plugin main file and supported WordPress and PHP versions before requesting changes.
Ask for verification steps that match the test tools available in the repository.
Review generated changes with WordPress coding standards and plugin-specific manual checks.
anti_patterns: Requesting broad site changes without naming the target plugin.
Skipping nonce, capability, sanitization, or escaping requirements for admin flows.
Removing data during uninstall without confirming the intended cleanup scope.

faq.question: Can this skill create a WordPress plugin from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline files and implement a starting plugin structure when repository context is available.

faq.question: Does it help with WordPress security requirements?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes nonces, capability checks, sanitization, escaping, prepared SQL, and careful request handling.

faq.question: Can it update an existing plugin?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect the plugin entry point, follow current structure, and make focused changes.

faq.question: Does it require WP-CLI?
faq.answer: No. Some debugging and verification tasks benefit from WP-CLI, but many code reviews do not require it.

faq.question: Does it replace official WordPress plugin review?
faq.answer: No. It supports development and review, but official requirements and human review still apply.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
